key_insight: Equivariant graph neural networks capture 3D geometry more effectively than rotation-invariant models, improving optical spectra prediction for materials screening.
engineering_relevance: Better spectra and static permittivity prediction can accelerate high-throughput discovery of optoelectronic materials, including candidates for solar cell and thin-film applications.
method: Adapted GotenNet into an equivariant GNN for optical spectra prediction.
Evaluated the model on multiple datasets, including a new 10,533-structure RPA spectra collection.
Compared against current state-of-the-art surrogate models for spectral prediction.
evidence_signal: The model outperformed prior methods, with the strongest improvements in the 0–8 eV spectral range and for static real permittivity.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown on benchmark datasets, so practical deployment still depends on transferability to new chemistries and spectrum calculation settings.
paper_title: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks Improve Optical Spectra Prediction for Materials Screening
